archetype.name: Playoff Team (defense-first, short-handed)
archetype.definition: A team whose top-five defense and star guard keep it comfortably in the playoff picture while injuries to key forwards hold its offense down near the league's middle.

report.headline: Elite rim defense and Gilgeous-Alexander are carrying a thinned-out offense
report.take:
Oklahoma City is 9-5 and 13th on the site, a long way from the 68-14 champion and 64-18 team of the last two years. Most of that drop is on one side of the floor. The defense is still elite, fifth with a 108.7 DRtg, and opponents' Opp Rim FG % of 56.7 is the best in the league, far below the league's 65.1. The offense is 16th with a 113.9 ORtg, after it sat seventh with 118.9 last season. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren have played three games each and are both listed out. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is carrying the load with a 36.4 USG % and an 8.4 BPM.

The shape of the offense has changed with the injuries. The 3PA Rate is 35.4, 29th in the league and down from 42.6 last season. The FT Rate of 24.6 ranks 26th. What keeps it afloat is ball security: a TOV % of 11.8, third best, means the Thunder rarely give away possessions even when they can't make shots. The guard rotation splits clearly. Ajay Mitchell has a +7.7 On-Off and 2.9 BPM, while Jared McCain has played more minutes with a -2.3 BPM and -5.1 On-Off. Isaiah Hartenstein (3.4 BPM, +4.9 On-Off) is the frontcourt anchor holding the rim together without Holmgren.

The record is honest. W vs Pt Diff sits at 0, and the margin implies exactly nine wins. The 5-5 last 10 looks worse than the play: the losses were on the road at Dallas, Houston, Portland twice and a one-point game at the Clippers, and the last five games still carry a +6.0 margin despite a 2-3 record. November's offense, at 116.38 a game against 106.5 in October, is the real sign of life.

The floor is high because the defense travels and Gilgeous-Alexander is a top-five guard on the site. The ceiling depends on when the injured forwards return. Until then this is a good team, not a dominant one, and the 53-win pace looks like a fair reading of it.

strengths.title: League's best rim protection
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 56.7 at the rim, first in the league and 8.4 points under the league average, and they get there less often than most. Opposing centers score well under their own averages against this team, the best mark in the league on that measure. Hartenstein's +4.9 On-Off is the engine without Holmgren. A defense that ranked first in each of the last two seasons has a strong track record, so this should last.

strengths.title: Gilgeous-Alexander's heavy, efficient load
strengths.body: He is fourth on the PG tab with 433 points in 14 games, a 58.7 TS % on a 36.4 USG %, and an 8.4 BPM. He is the reason a thinned offense still sits mid-league rather than near the bottom. That much usage is sustainable for him, but it leaves little margin when he sits.

strengths.title: Protecting the ball
strengths.body: A TOV % of 11.8 ranks third and sits well under the league. That fits this team's history, with a low turnover rate in each of its recent seasons. It is a structural trait, and it gives a short-handed offense extra possessions to work with.

concerns.title: An offense without spacing
concerns.body: The 3PA Rate has fallen to 35.4, 29th in the league, from 42.6 last season, and eFG % is 51.9 against the league's 53.5. With Jalen Williams and Holmgren out, the shooting and secondary creation are thin. The ORtg of 113.9 is the clearest gap between this team and the last two. It should improve when they return, but there's no return date in the sheet.

concerns.title: Wing defense leaks
concerns.body: Small forwards score above their own averages against OKC and hit more threes over their norms than against any other defense in the league. The wing group is down to depth minutes with Jalen Williams out. It is the one weak spot in an otherwise excellent defense.

concerns.title: Guard rotation split
concerns.body: McCain has the second-most backcourt minutes but a -2.3 BPM and -5.1 On-Off. Mitchell is +7.7 with a 2.9 BPM. How the minutes are split behind Gilgeous-Alexander matters more than usual with the forwards out.

trend.note: October's offense scored only 106.5 a game, and November's 116.38 shows it finding footing even short-handed. The 5-5 last 10 came mostly on the road, and the last five still carry a +6.0 margin.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games, then a Florida-Indiana back-to-back against weaker teams
weekAhead.body:
After a road-heavy stretch, OKC gets Atlanta and New Orleans at home, then Miami and Indiana on consecutive nights. All four opponents sit below the Thunder on the site. New Orleans has the league's worst defense at a 121.2 DRtg, and Indiana's wing and frontcourt groups both grade D-.

The matchups favor what OKC does. Atlanta and New Orleans both rank in the bottom five at protecting the rim, which helps a team that can't shoot its way to points right now. Miami gives up threes at the second-worst rate in the league. The danger game is Atlanta: an A+ wing group against OKC's weakest defensive position, and the league's second-best defense at forcing turnovers.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta's wings vs a thin rotation
keyMatchups.body: The Hawks' wings grade A+, and OKC's defense lets small forwards beat their own averages more than most. Atlanta also forces turnovers at the second-highest rate, though OKC's ball security ranks third. The home opener of the week is the likeliest loss.

keyMatchups.title: Guard scoring against soft perimeters
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows shooting guards the most over their averages in the league, at +7.09. Miami allows point guards 31.92 a game and ranks 29th against shooting guards. That sets up Gilgeous-Alexander and Mitchell for big nights.

keyMatchups.title: Rim attacks vs porous interiors
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans allows a 71.4 Opp Rim FG %, 29th, and Atlanta allows 69.1, 26th. An offense that lives inside the arc gets its best looks of the season here. New Orleans' league-leading FT Rate is the one way it could hang around.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Jalen Williams or Holmgren returns, and how the offense holds up on the second night of the Miami-Indiana back-to-back.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense is the sustainable part: rim protection and ball security have been strengths for years, and there's no close-game luck to give back. The offense is the variable. At full strength, with Jalen Williams and Holmgren back, the three-point volume and efficiency should climb toward last season's levels, and the net rating should follow. Without them, this looks like a top-eight team rather than a title favorite.

With 68 games left, a final win total in the low-to-mid 50s fits both the current pace and the likelihood of better health later in the season. The defense should stay top five, with an ORtg of 114 to 118 depending on who returns.
swingFactors: Return dates for Jalen Williams and Holmgren

confidence.note: Fourteen games, a road-heavy start, and key forwards out with no timeline in the sheet.
